survey: A single tall brown leather cowboy boot, shown in side view with the toe pointing right. It has four parts. The shaft is a tall, slightly flared tube with a scalloped top and a visible tan lining. It sits on a stitched lower foot section (heel counter and vamp), and the seam where they join reads clearly. The pointed toe rests on a thin dark sole that runs the full length of the foot. A dark, blocky, slightly angled heel is fixed under the back of the sole, and its back edge lines up with the counter. There is no ground plane, so the boot is a floating icon, which is normal for a card. A gold spur sits at the back of the heel, just above the heel stack. A star rowel is mounted on a hub at the end of a short shank behind the boot. The heel band curves forward from the shank along the near side of the counter and ends in a rounded tip at about mid-heel. That reads as the near arm of the U-shaped band, with the far arm hidden behind the boot. No spur strap or buckle crosses the instep to hold the spur on.

errors.where: Gold spur heel band, rounded tip against the side of the boot counter
errors.what: The spur's heel band stops in a bare rounded tip on the leather. There is no strap button, and no spur strap runs over the instep and under the arch, so nothing holds the spur on the boot. It looks glued to the side of the heel rather than strapped on.

fix: Make the spur's heel band a U that wraps around the back of the boot heel. Put a small button on the end of each arm, and run a leather spur strap from the buttons over the top of the instep, ideally buckled, so the spur is visibly strapped to the boot.
